analysis:
The PR changes documentation only; no source implementation was supplied.

Main change, in docs/reference/configuration.md head 923-1002: the release lane registers `cluster_runtime` (schema v2, up to 64 models) in POST /v1/releases. The coordinator derives build-pinned approvals, grants and parity qualifications from it. Declared models (GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B) get self-declared promotable qualifications that apply family-wide on any Apple silicon. This is flagged as a gap against A-017/T-054 (qualification independence) and A-005 (release key scope).

The coordinator-side acceptance and validation of the block lives in darkbloom-platform and is outside the evidence. Integration should verify whether derived qualifications need a separate operator approval.

Other changes, not flagged:
- Qwen27 TP speculative assistant: local-only by default; with mtp_mode=on the pair is not offered. ClusterConfiguration refuses tensorAssistant beside nativeMember (config 1102, 1635-1636; two-mac 77-94). This reduces public exposure.
- Constrained JSON refusal on Qwen pairs, with coordinator failover (two-mac 96-104).
- Approval fallback: coordinator-decided ends are not counted, and a set-aside approval is retried after 3600 s (config 1102; two-mac 182-191). This is availability only.
- Manual update guidance (two-mac 524-552).

The local API binding to all interfaces without TLS (two-mac 254-260) is unchanged, pre-existing text. The prefix-cache per-tenant scoping text (T-041) is unchanged.

Open questions:
- Does the request_envelope maximum of 1,048,576 tokens rely on worker limits for DoS bounds?
- Is the GLM schedule-2 approval actually inert, as line 996 claims?

findings.detail: Head lines 923-936 and 965-993 say a signed release now sends `cluster_runtime` in `POST /v1/releases`. From that block, the coordinator derives the build's cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. For declared models the qualifications are fixed by the build: `promotable=true`, `diverged=false`, a constant `qualified_at`, and evidence that is only the hash of an owner-decision report. The coordinator then applies them to the whole mode family on any numerics class, cut and share split. Line 992-993 admits that GLM-5.3-Flash has no tensor-parallel cross-cable record and that neither model ran pipeline on two M5 Ultras. So whoever holds the release key (A-005) can publish a build that grants itself public pair-serving qualification. This moves qualification from durable, independently approved records (A-017, T-054) into the release-publication channel. It also widens public exposure to shapes that never passed parity, weakening the T-007 output-integrity argument. Trigger: a release with the environment variable on is registered, and the coordinator accepts the block. Impact: public consumer traffic is routed to untested pair placements. Fix: keep parity qualification separate from release registration, with independent approval and cross-cable records per numerics-class combination. Alternatively, record this explicitly in the threat model as an accepted risk under A-017/T-054/TB-011.
findings.title: Release-carried parity qualifications admit public cluster traffic without independent cross-cable evidence
